text: Welcome everyone. Welcome to Sunbird CIC week, and thank you all for joining today's investor meeting with Zhen Ding Technology. Today we have President Jeff Chen, Sales Manager Alan Chen, Spokesman Dun, and Vivi Chang, IR Specialist. Now I turn the floor to the company. Thank you.

Hello, thank you so much for having us here. We will have a brief introduction about Zhen Ding, and then we will have a brief video for everyone to know our smart fab, and after that we will have Q&A time for everyone.

This is a brief introduction about Zhen Ding, and we are the global number one PCB manufacturer for sequential nine years. And you can see from the revenue part, this 182 billion we have reached the record high last year, and this year will also reach record high, especially you can see from the first half year's revenue report. Because this year our key driver will be the AI servers, substrate, optical and edge AI.

Especially this part, the revenue has ramped up really quick from the first half year, the sampling degree and small mass production. Second half will be even more. And next year our CapEx devotion will start it to ramp, especially for new fabs will start to develop more capacity for high-end AI PCB.

You can see from this red pie chart, the server, optical module and IC substrate, last year for full year is only accounted 11.7%, but this year's first half has accounted 21.6%. And till the end of 2026, we expect this part will reach 25%, and till 2027, this part will reach 30%.

And this is the recent business update. For the first half, our high-margin product, especially server, transceiver, substrate, the YoY has reached 113% YoY and accounted 21.6%. Also for revenue part, also reached the record high.

You can see from our first half's gross margin and operating margin has come to a really quite different grade compared to the same period with last year. And for this growing cycle for high-end PCB, we can see this is a new opportunity and new phase for us, and this year is just a beginning for momentum for us. And this life cycle will gain more 40 to 50 billion revenue this year, and after this cycle till 2030, we think that this growing phase will still continue.

For next phase, growing through industrial capacity expansion, we have raised our capital expenditure to 80 billion in this year, and have 22 new fabs under construction, and another 9 planned in the planning stage. So adding our original 28 fabs, we will have 59 fabs develop the revenue in the end of 2030.

And for fundraising plan, we have Leading Interconnect Semiconductor Technology and has submitted the IPO application in the Hong Kong stock market in July 2nd in this year, and the IPO stage will finish targeted next year's Q1.

And this is a business overview. For the optical module, we only targeted high-end optical module like 800G and 1.6T, and afterwards 3.2T, NPO and CPO are still under sampling stage. And after the capital expenditure has expanded more capacity for us, we have targeted to become the world largest supplier for high-end optical module PCB by next year.

And AI server part, we have targeted high-end GPU and ASIC customers, and for this year we have small production for them, and for the next 2 to 3 generations we will expand more capacity for them, especially in 2027 and 2028.

For edge AI, even though this year is not a really good year for consumer-grade product, but this part we still see a low to mid-single-digit growth, because from the big customer the unit didn't drop that much, and especially for ASP we can transfer for the upstream suppliers ASP raise, and especially for the customer we can have more space for negotiation.

This is SEMICON Taiwan this year, and we have showcased 800G and 1.6T mass production product, and also have the next generation's XPO and NPO applications. For AI server, we have launched our high-end HDI product and has up to 34 layers. This part is also the sector of our biggest capacity has devoted into.

This is the Prismark research, and you can see it's totally different from this decade 2020 to 2030, the CAGR has goes up to 9.5%, and this kind of shortage it also shows from our customer's demand, and also the market scale is following this trend. And especially from the high-end PCB and also IC substrate, the shortage we can see it is still shortage in 2028, and also our booking phase has come to 2028, we have no more capacity for even more new customers.

And here, how we engage with AI: we have more especially focused on edge AI before, because for last year it's up to almost 90% of consumer-grade product. But this year we will have more focus on AI server and optical module. And after 5 years, we can see there is even more opportunity in physical AI part, especially for vehicles and robots. And this part we have started to engage with customers and started sampling-degree new product.

So we want to build a One ZDT platform, that we didn't transfer consumer-grade products' HDI and IC substrate move to AI infrastructure, it's because consumer degrees' customer, the demand is still strong and we have a long-term partnership with them. So we will not remove their product line to new customer just because we see the trend is even higher margin. We really precious this kind of relationship with our big customer, but we want to engage more in the new trend like AI infrastructure. So our new capacity will be more focused on high-end HDI, HLC, and IC substrate, and more new customer is starting to engage in here.

And this is the revenue target. From 2010, we have targeted ourselves to earn more 10 billion each year. This year will be a lot of difference, we have gained 40 to 50 billion more this year, and afterwards will be following this trend, and we believe it will be even more.

Here is we have host the global supplier conference in Shenzhen in July 24. You can see there are 247 suppliers come to our activity, no matter from glass or copper or even facilities, drilling suppliers, they have all come to join with us. And many investors might ask about upstream supplier shortage problem, but actually we can tell that this year's upstream materials we have booked from 2024 to 2025. So for this year and next year, we are not in that kind of shortage. We are negotiate with them for the material in 2029 to 2030. So if you ask if it is in shortage, it is, but for this year or next year we have no gap to supply our material for the downstream customers.

Here is the optical module demand from Yole Group research. Many investors will argue about when NPO and CPO has appeared, the pluggable might disappear. But actually you can see from this chart, next year and also in 2028, even though NPO and CPO has started, pluggable usage is still strong, because we can see from second-tier or third-tier CSP customers, no matter from cost or you want to fix your rack, optical module will be a lot cheaper than NPO and CPO. So we think this trend follows this chart.

For the unit in optical module market, we have more focus on 800G, 1.6T and 3.2T. In this year's shipping units, 800G will exceed 1.6T, but from revenue part, it will be 50 to 50. And next year, no matter unit part or revenue, 1.6T will increase even higher and strongly exceed 800G.

This is a brief roadmap from GPU server and ASIC server. Many investors might worry about oversupply issue, but you can see no matter from next generation's product, technology degree or layer count of PCB or surface of PCB, this will use a lot of our capacity. In this chart we can see the shortage will not stop till 2028, and for 2029 to 2030 we are still checking, but we can see shortage will not stop. Especially from ASP part, Goldman research shows in next year ASP for tented part has come to this grade, and in 2028 comes to two times degree. So shortage will still continue even in 2029 to 2030.

And this is our technology capability in ABF substrate. We have suffered this part for many years, but this year we have break-even in Q1 and submitted our application for IPO in July 2nd. When our market scale and technology degree have goes even higher, our margin and revenue will expand really quick.

Server, optical and IC substrate percentage comes to 21.6%, and in 2030 we expect this part will come to 45 to 50%. But for actual number it will goes even higher in mass production and exceed consumer-grade product.

For expenditure, we have 22 new fabs under construction, 9 more fabs in planning stage. In Huai'an project, in the end of this year there will have 6 more new PCB fabs completed across different 3 campuses. And the 4th campus has break ground in April this year, also with high-end PCB, topped out by August 10, finish construction and commence production in next year's March.

In Shenzhen campus, campus 3 has break ground in July 2026, and will have 3 smart new fabs, also with high-end PCB. Leading Technology also break ground in this year's September, targeted high-end ABF product.

For Thailand Fab 1, it is also targeted high-end HDI and has mass production in last year's 3Q, and because ramp up went really smooth, this year's July has achieved break-even. There are 4 more new fabs has finished construction, expected to commence from this year's 4th Q, and next year's 1st Q we expected to have small mass production.

This is Huai'an campus, built to become the world largest PCB campus. Here is Shenzhen campus, Campus 3 break ground in this year's July, Leading Campus 2 break ground in this year's September. And Thailand campus, PA01 has contributed revenue currently, broke even in July. 4 new fabs, the blue part, finished construction, and L02 and 06 will go even fast for high-end AI PCB.

For our different subsidiaries, we have more focus on China because of manpower or government support, we have more efficiency. But this year we have come to have more international customers, so we have aggressive plan especially in Thailand and Kaohsiung.

For smart fab, this is key for why we can have 22 new fabs under construction at the same time, even in different country like Thailand. We benchmark the level of smart fab with semiconductor, so even if you go to TSMC fab you can see this kind of level of smart fab. That is why we want to build new fab instead of buying old fab, because for future high-end PCB we need this kind of smart manufacturing level to fulfill customer need.

Here is R&D expenses. This year's first half has slightly higher than before, but for full year we will diluted into 6 to 8%. Payout ratio remains 50%. For ESG part, we have valued this part for more than 10 years, and we will improve our rating in the future.

For financial results, compared to same period last year we have better performance, especially gross margin, operating margin and net margin. But for expenses we have higher than before because of CapEx devoted into new fab construction and manpower, but for full year we will diluted to 12 to 13%. For depreciation, we will start from mass production, so for full year will goes slightly higher for 10 to 15% and comes to 22 billion NT dollars.

This is quarterly operation results. Last year we have 88% consumer-grade products, so we suffer off-season and peak-season. But this year, many mass production comes to second half, so it will still look the same, but for next year or 2028 we can remain in a high UT rate.

Balance sheet: even though capital expenditure has come to record high this year, cash flow and liabilities still remain in a really healthy rate. We also have three different fundraising plans: ZDT has ECB 6, Avary has fundraising plan, and Leading Technology has IPO ongoing, in preparation for next year's capital expenditure.

For the last 10 years, revenue steadily goes upward. Even though CapEx goes to record high, for risk we have down to a really low phase because no matter downstream customer or upstream supplier, we have signed LTA with customer. So if you ask the risk, for this year we have the highest phase of capital expenditure, but the lowest risk for us. Thank you, is there any question?
How about margin in terms of what targets you might have internally as the AI business continues to grow? Gross margins for each product sector?

Let me introduce our gross margin by different sectors. Actually the consumer computers compared to server, optical and IC substrate, right now these red parts is higher than consumer grade. That is why normally first half is low season, first half and second half gross margin gap around 5 to 8 percentage points, but this year the gap is shortened. Looking at product sectors, actually for the last couple of years, HDI is most high profit margins, come after FPC, and last couple of years IC substrate, server product is under development. We just turn around from low profit margin into much higher than corporate average from this year. That is why this year is tremendous first year, we targeted to have more IC substrates high margins, and optical margin is even higher.

Right now the margin ranking, first is optical module right now, and come after IC substrate, server AI, and consumer computers come after. Smartphone take the biggest for last couple of years, almost 60%, but this year will come to around 50%. This kind of product portfolio changing is good for Zhen Ding's next growing drivers.
How much is the margin of the server optical module and IC substrate, and how much is for the mobile application?

We did not disclose one by one, we only introduce by prioritize or ranking of gross margins each sectors. Roughly optical module right now is over 40-50%, is most high profitability, high profit margins. Come after IC substrate, especially ABF, because last couple of years ABF suffering under UT rate, but right now our first fab already fully utilized, and Fab 2 under installations. Because IC substrate kind of shortage, all upstream cost already pass through to end customer's ASP.
When you talk about doubling the capacity by 2030, shall we have any concern on the margin side? For the capacity expansion, will it be a drag on the margins?
Not in the near term.
For new plant setup, how fast can it ramp up the production?
For the construction to installation to certification mass production, within 2 to 3 years.
So a new plant need to have 2 to 3 years, and then come to a full production?
Yes.
So by 2030, there's 59 plants in total, more than double. Is there a case that in 2030, what if by the end of 2030 all the demand is gone?

Actually we give you a 5 years foresight, but after that actually we are seeing continuously to expanding. And the overall trend for this AI-driven combined with semiconductor and other demand is still very strong. For the period of time from new factory construction to mass production is normally 2 to 3 years, and we build the new factory first, it's like a real option. So we can based on the demand to pull in our installation as well as for mass production. But this kind of investment give us the capacity to fulfill various demand from our customer, and most of those demand they have long-term agreement and prepaid contract etc.
How long will be the contract?

3 to 5 years right now, because of the shortage for the longer term period of time. Especially substrate, server AI, optical module, these red sectors. PCB industry linked to semiconductors, PCB connect tightly with semiconductors because of the form factors, high efficiency performance, energy performance, so they highly leverage the PCB advantage to combine with their product design. That is 2 to 3 years in China, but in Taiwan or Japan at least 3 to 4 years. That is why everybody facing the shortage in such a longer period of time, because it takes time.

You can see the small words under that, it's already ongoing. That says that 59 will be total finished. Depends on the customer situation, each factory, each catalog will be different. We believe that the specification of each product will be changed again in upcoming years.

If you see the numbers here is the TAM of the PCB industry by Prismark. Why we follow the numbers of them, they update that by each quarter, you can see that in 2030 the numbers compared to last year is almost double. That's just simply revenue-wise, the global TAM number. If you see our expansion and whole industry expansion, actually the expansion is not doubled yet. Yes, we have confidence that the demand will not be drop, it's driven by the AI infrastructure. All the Magnificent Seven in these two months, they announced again their CapEx investment will be double, triple in the next coming 3 to 5 years. So currently we don't have to worry about that.

Question on the substrate business. Right now the current situation is tight, margins are expanding. Do you have a view on how many quarters see that expansion? What's the pace of the pricing increases?

As my colleague Dun just mentioned, the investment of new factory, especially for IC substrates close to semiconductors, take longer lead time. So the gap between demand and supply is still large. So you can foresee the price will still maintain a healthy growth, and it is good to contribute our margin and our profit structure.
Generally speaking, for the market, do we see gross margins go beyond past peak levels for the industry, just given how tight things are?

PCB industry is so transparent, no matter demand or supply, but all of a sudden the demand changing very fast due to the high-end application, new material, new machinery, new design comes in to PCB industry. So the most important is our strategy is One ZDT, one-stop shop. Our advantage by using smart fab, not only used by IC substrate, but also HDI, mSAP, FPC. The other thing is pricing strategies, raw material price hike, no matter T-glass, E-glass, CCL, copper foil, drilling bits, all these key components and high-end supply shortage. Because of such kind of bottleneck, we pass through the product price to our end demand.

Usually consumer has more bargaining power, but AI industry is so different. PCB takes a very low percentage of BOM cost, but it drives a key performance for their AI data center or downstream applications. So they are willing to accept price adapt higher cost upstream. That's why we think there's not much worry about margin expansion, and we take advantage of margin expansion in 2 to 3 years, because we invest a lot on R&D combined with upstream and downstream customers.
What is the share of server and IC substrate?
The first half around 10%, and Q3 up to 12%.
What is the status in ABF next step?

The ABF, we have Fab 2 installation stage and fully booked by our customers. Because of shortage, we kick off new fab construction last month to keep expansion. The new campus for ABF substrate, there is additional 3 to 4 new fab will be ongoing for expansion.
How about price?
Substrate is the most one of shortage conditions, so the price fully reflects all the upstream costs and substrate costs. That's why the margin keep expansion as well.
How about BT?
If you look at the A1 submission in Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the BT, first Q of BT is higher than ABF, but right now third Q, I think ABF already keeping up.
Are we converting any BT capacity to ABF?
Not really. Like Vivi mentioned, we focus keep expansion on our new fab instead of transfer the BT into ABF.
When is Fab 2 for substrate going to ramp?
Q1 next year.
Do you have guidance for next year's growth for substrate and server?
Not really, but by our expansion capacities, it shall double ABF compared to this year, because one fab become two. Probably more than double, yes.
Any question from online?

Can I squeeze in a quick question?
Sorry, we cannot see the video online. Need you to share screen, thanks.
There we go, thank you.

From Pengshen's inception, our factory was designed as a high-quality, high-efficiency, and energy-smart facility. Every aspect of the layout was meticulously planned around optimized production workflows. The entire facility operates under cleanroom standards, with graded cleanliness zones tailored to specific manufacturing requirements. The facility implements a Class 1000 cleanroom. Adapting semiconductor-level intelligence, our Manufacturing Execution System (MES) serves as the central hub, seamlessly integrating ERP, EAP, APS, AMHS, QMS, WMS, Traceability, and other related systems.

100% equipment connectivity with automated recipe deployment by EAP. Full process traceability through unique 2D codes assigned at material unloading, linking raw materials, fixtures, and product data. Leveraging SEMI SECS/GEM protocols, real-time production data and equipment parameter monitoring. Automated visual management of panel handling systems. Cross-floor AGV material transport activated by production line requests. Centralized command system synthesizes real-time operational data with predictive analytics for rapid executive decision-making. End-to-end traceability from design to delivery.

Just like the video shows, this new factory in Thailand, our subsidiary company in Thailand, they adopt smart manufacturing, smart fab at once. So even in Thailand we need to face the challenge of multiple-nation employee, but still the speed for ramp-up, the quality, yield and profitability is much better than our competitors. We adopt this smart factory for all new factories under construction, those 29 factories. For high-end market customer, you need the semiconductor standard for yield and quality reliability, so smart factory is our competitive advantage.
Is there any bottleneck for execution of the factory, say raw material or equipment?

We maintain long-term partnership with our supply chain partners. Demand is so high so everyone tried to get more resource, but the leader like us will get more resource than the others. That's why we are confident for this expansion, not just long-term agreement with customer, we also have MOU and similar arrangement with our partners.
Which part is the shortage? Supply chain or the equipment part? Any lead time of equipment waiting for very long?
Several machinery equipments are long lead time delivery over 12 to 18 months. That is why upon the LTA confirmed, we shall have MOU agreement with equipment suppliers.

Because we have so longer plan to build new factory, so for those long lead time bottleneck equipment, we issue our order much earlier than the others. We need to synchronize the installation time. Maybe bottleneck to the others, but for us it is not. We issue PO, PR based on the right timing.
We prepay or we placing order in advance.
That's why I say we synchronize the time for the arrival.
One question on T-glass supply. What are we doing there to secure more supply, given some suppliers prioritize existing clients?

We are using similar strategies. We confirm with the order from clients, and we also confirm with supplier by not only one CCL, but so many. Different CCL vendors are focusing different advantage for their own. Like TaiGlass, Nittobo should be the first one, most high-end, but we also certificate different vendors like Taiwan Glass, Grace in China, and for CCL not only Doosan, EMC, but also many, up to 8 to 10 CCL suppliers. No matter T-glass or E-glass, it's still price hike, these kind of shortage seems not easy to sufficient supply yet. Like Jeff mentioned, synchronize the demand and supply, fully support transparency of price, so we can smoothly keep expansion and keep getting market share.

For the supplier, they will also select their customer, not just based on surge demand, they will also consider long-term relationship. In some situation, our customer will bring us and supplier together to make sure those demand and supply is synchronized. Even though a lot of people try to tracing those materials, they also need to justify. Company like Zhen Ding, we have long-term partnership with customer and supplier, sustainable growth plan, transparent and reliable financial planning, that customer can trust us and supplier can trust us too.
When there is incremental supply coming, they had to decide whether to give it to, how does that decision get made by suppliers, how much to give to various players?

The supplier, they select their customer based on partnership, based on long-term relationship. Zhen Ding, we maintain very close partnership with all ecosystem. As this slide illustrated, so many important suppliers in this ecosystem come to join us. Our Chairman, our COO, we visit our supplier regularly, exchange information, help to maintain a healthy growth for the whole ecosystem. Supplier will finally judge which one is more reliable, sustainable, in the long-term partnership.
Our time is out, so that's conclude today's investment meeting with Zhen Ding Technology. Thank you management team, and thank you investors in person and online. Thank you.
Thank you very much.
